quizzes.stem: A coordinator spends ten turns investigating a failing build, then tells a subagent only to "fix the broken check". The subagent opens other modules and edits the wrong one. What should the coordinator have done?

options.a: Put the file's location and the error text into its prompt
options.b: Let the subagent look up the parent's earlier tool results in the session
options.c: Name a stronger model for the subagent in its definition file
options.d: Have a second subagent review every edit before it is saved

explanation.a: The subagent's context starts fresh, so the brief is the only channel for facts the coordinator already found.
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing is inherited: "The only content you pass from parent to subagent is the Agent tool's prompt string".
explanation.c: Ruled out because a stronger model still lacks the facts, and "a vague brief produces vague work."
explanation.d: Ruled out because a reviewing subagent starts from the same bare brief and cannot tell which edit is wrong: "If a fact is not in the brief, the subagent does not have it".

quizzes.stem: A team plans a multi-agent design for a feature built in three steps. Each step needs what the step before it found, and the user redirects the work after every step. Which choice fits best?

options.a: Chain three fixed prompts that run end to end without a pause
options.b: Give each step to its own subagent
options.d: Add a coordinator that merges what the three step-agents produce at the end

explanation.c: Each step builds on the last and the user steers between them, so the work keeps one context and stays open to the user.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the documentation lists this case for the main conversation: "multiple phases share significant context, such as planning, implementation, and testing".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a fixed chain leaves no room for the user's redirection, and the task "needs frequent back-and-forth or iterative refinement".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the dependencies are the problem: "some domains that require all agents to share the same context or involve many dependencies between agents are not a good fit".

quizzes.stem: A subagent's call is cut short by a rate limit, and the coordinator's synthesis quotes the line "API error: rate limited" as if it were a finding. What should the coordinator do instead?

options.a: Hand the error line to the synthesizer as a low-confidence finding
options.b: Return a partial status that lists the unfinished scope as missing
options.c: Instruct the synthesizer to skip any sentence that looks like an error
options.d: Send the whole team out again until every subagent succeeds

explanation.b: A failure belongs to its scope, and the user is owed a list of what is missing.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a caveat does not change what the line is: "A failure is never turned into a finding."
explanation.c: Ruled out because the problem is then hidden: "A partial answer looks like a full one".
explanation.d: Ruled out because it is the other coordinator mistake: "Sending every brief out again in the next round doubles the cost and adds repeats".

quizzes.stem: After its first wave of subagents the lead finds that two of five sections are weak. It sends every assignment out again, and the bill doubles with little new content. Which change fits best?

options.a: Resend each assignment once more, then stop after that single extra round
options.b: Start a larger first wave so that fewer parts come back thin
options.c: Let the synthesis step fill the weak sections from what the model already knows
options.d: Brief fresh workers only on the gaps the review named, under a round cap

explanation.d: The review names the gaps, only they are sent out again, and the rounds are capped.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a larger wave raises the price of every section, the three sound ones included, when each wave must earn its cost: "multi-agent systems require tasks where the value of the task is high enough to pay for the increased performance."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "a gap is found by the review and closed by a subagent, never invented by the synthesis."
explanation.a: Ruled out because even one extra round repeats work that is already done: "the first-round findings are already in hand".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator splits each research question across search, analysis and synthesis subagents and returns a cited report. On one question, two of the three subagents come back with almost the same findings on the same period. Which cause fits best?

options.a: The coordinator ran too few rounds of review after the first answers
options.b: The context of one subagent leaked into another during the run
options.c: The briefs did not say what ground each one had to leave out
options.d: The subagents ran on a smaller model than the coordinator uses

explanation.c: Overlap comes from the brief, because the subagents cannot see each other.
explanation.b: Ruled out because nothing crosses between subagents: "A subagent does not know the user's original question, the plan, the other subagents".
explanation.a: Ruled out because review cannot undo duplicate work already paid for, and the page puts the cause in the briefs: "Without detailed task descriptions, agents duplicate work, leave gaps, or fail to find necessary information."
explanation.d: Ruled out because no model of any size sees the other briefs, and the page warns against "hoping that the model will see what its siblings are doing, because it cannot".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator splits each research question across search, analysis and synthesis subagents and returns a cited report. The coordinator starts the same five subagents for every query, including "what is the boiling point of water". Which redesign fits best?

options.a: Keep the five subagents but lower the token limit of each one
options.b: Scale the team to the difficulty of each task
options.c: Let the five subagents work in one shared context
options.d: Start the team only when the user asks for a long report

explanation.b: The effort should follow the question: "Simple fact-finding requires just 1 agent with 3-10 tool calls".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a lower limit still starts the whole team for the plain fact: "A fixed team runs on every query and costs most on the simplest".
explanation.c: Ruled out because sharing does not shrink the team's work and undoes the isolation: "it removes the isolation that keeps the context small".
explanation.d: Ruled out because the length of a report is not the difficulty of the question, and "the coordinator chooses which subagents to invoke from the complexity of the query".

quizzes.stem: Scenario S3, a multi-agent research system. A coordinator splits each research question across search, analysis and synthesis subagents and returns a cited report. Specialist agents hand forty-page drafts up through the coordinator, and the cost of each run climbs with every handoff, yet the final report must keep every detail from those drafts. Which architecture change fits best?

options.a: Cap the number of turns each specialist may take
options.b: Have the coordinator condense each draft before relaying it
options.c: Give every specialist a full copy of the coordinator's conversation
options.d: Write each output to a store and pass on a pointer

explanation.d: A reference keeps the output out of the lead's window and out of its summaries.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the coordinator still reads each full draft, so it "pays for each token twice", and it "loses detail at every summary".
explanation.c: Ruled out because copying through conversation history is the cost: "reduces token overhead from copying large outputs through conversation history".
explanation.a: Ruled out because a cap on turns does not change where the drafts travel, and the lead still reads each one: "Rather than requiring subagents to communicate everything through the lead agent".
